text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Outgoing Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan proposed a coalition with secularist Mesut Yilmaz before he announced his resignation. Prime minister-designate Yilmaz rejected the offer.
- Turkish television exports, aimed chiefly at European Union countries, rose 70 percent in the first five months of the year to 782,000.
- Erbakan is to attend on Wednesday his final meeting of the powerful National Security Council, whose anti-Islamist demands sparked the crisis in his government.
- An Islamist company's down payment for a tyre company is to be frozen in the course of an investigation into its activities.
- Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit makes an appeal to Tansu Ciller, allied with Islamists, to join a secularist coalition.
- The mass housing administration has not paid debts of 431 billion lira in connection with a United Nations conference on human settlements last year.
- The mood of the economy perks up. The stock exchange has moved to record levels since free-marketeer Yilmaz was asked to form a government.
- A textile company has lost the right to buy state bank Etibank after it failed to make the necessary downpayment.
- The National Security Council meeting will present Erbakan proposals on Islamic associations and companies.
- The Islamist Welfare Party's decision to expel three deputies is a move to counter a constitutional court case aimed at closing the party, lawyers say.

- An MP resigning from the conservative True Path Party says he will not be followed by more than three more deputies. Yilmaz would need support of around a dozen True Path deputies to win support for a secularist coalition.
